Fixture: every indented line below has to be refused by the rule
no-absolute-home-path in .github/invariants.txt.

This file is excluded from the scan of the tree, because it holds the violation
on purpose. What it proves is that the rule still bites, which nothing else in
the run would notice: the tree is clean either way, so a pattern that lost an
alternative would go green over it.

The four shapes, one per line. Nothing here is a path anybody has.

    C:\Users\example\src\reissbrett\notes.md
    c:\Users\example\src\reissbrett\notes.md
    /home/example/src/reissbrett/notes.md
    /Users/example/src/reissbrett/notes.md

The second line is the one the effort went into. A lowercase drive letter is
what an editor's autocomplete produces and what a reader's eye reads as the
uppercase one, and a rule written to match only the uppercase form passes it.

Every other line in this file is prose and the rule has to match none of it,
which the run also asserts: it compares the line numbers that matched against
the line numbers that are indented and requires the two sets to be equal.
